The global phase change materials market was estimated at USD 2.6 billion in 2024. The market is expected to grow from USD 3 billion in 2025 to USD 7.9 billion in 2034, at a CAGR of 11.4%, according to latest report published by Global Market Insights Inc.

Construction and building industries maintain the highest demand in PCM consumption with about 40 % of the total consumption, while electronics cooling and automotive thermal management segments are likely to exhibit growth above 17% CAGR in forecast year.

Inorganic PCMs including salt hydrates and nitrate salts are expanding rapidly with 11.9% CAGR growth, mainly in the area of industrial waste-heat recovery and solar thermal energy storage. Issues associating with the category such as corrosion remain, however, encapsulation methods are developing to improve lifecycle performance.

The composite and hybrid PCM segment is poised to take record high growth with a 17.9% CAGR, as microencapsulated and polymer-stabilized systems become increasingly common for thermal management in electronics, electric vehicles, and textiles. Shape-stabilized PCMs are also gaining traction with some innovative applications in aerospace and high-temperature environments.

High-temperature PCMs, including nitrate salts and fluoride salts, are advancing in solar thermal power and composting waste-heat recovery at 9.2% CAGR within the extensive decarbonization of industry.

The market for thermal management and control designs is growing at 10.6% CAGR and expanding due to opportunities in electronics cooling, electric vehicle battery management, and data center infrastructure. Comfort and conditioning are also expanding, largely due to trends in delivering sustainable urbanization opportunities.

The electronics and semiconductor segment is estimated to have a growth projection of 10.7% CAGR. Growing demand is attributable to device miniaturization and increased demand for thermal management in consumer electronics, data centers, and high-performance computing applications.
